 Who We Are & What We Do
Tallahassee Memorial HealthCare (TMH) is a private, nonprofit community-based healthcare system that provides advanced care to a 21-county region in North Florida and South Georgia. We are a career destination with nearly 6,000 colleagues who reflect the diversity of our community.
TMH is the region’s healthcare leader and top provider of advanced care with a 772-bed acute care hospital and the region’s only:
- Level II Trauma Center 
- Joint Commission Comprehensive Stroke Center 
- Level III Neonatal Intensive Care 
- Pediatric Intensive Care 
- The most advanced cancer, heart and vascular, orthopedic & surgery programs in the Panhandle 
Our system also includes a psychiatric hospital, multiple specialty care centers, four residency programs and nearly 40 affiliated physician practices.
How You'll Make An Impact
Location: Tallahassee, FL
As the Executive Director of IS Operations and Technology, you will play a pivotal role in the operational integrity, reliability, and continuous improvement of the health system's technology infrastructure and IS services. Serves as a key partner to clinical and business leaders; balances day-to-day operational excellence with strategic infrastructure planning to support a safe, efficient, and patient-centered care environment.
If you are a seasoned IT leader with a passion for technology innovation and a deep understanding of healthcare IT, we invite you to apply for this exciting opportunity! Join our dedicated team in using technology to revolutionize healthcare and positively impact patient outcomes.
The Executive Director of IS Operations and Technology is responsible for:
- Oversees all “Keep the Lights On” (KTLO)/“Run the Business” (RTB) activities; ensures clinical, administrative, and operational information systems remain available, secure, and performant 24 hours/day, 7days/week (“24/7”). 
- Collaborates with the security team to mitigate cybersecurity threats. 
- Leads and develops a team of IS managers, engineers, and support staff members. 
- Demonstrating integrity, compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence (I CARE values). 
- Communicates information timely via appropriate channels. 
- Displays an understanding of diversity. Manages departmental budget. Meet goals/expectations established over the previous year. 
- Manages human resources. 
- Meets or exceeds all The Joint Commission (TJC) requirements. 
- Solves problems; recommends sound solutions. 
- Enhances and contributes to a safe environment for all colleagues, visitors, and patients. 
Reports to:
- Chief Information Officer/VP 
Supervises:
- Director/IT Infrastructure Services 
- Director/IT Planning and Quality 
What You’ll Need To Apply
Education:
- Required: Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, or a related healthcare field; 
- Preffered: Master's degree. 
Experience: 
- Minimum of ten (10) years of healthcare IT and operations experience (including five (5) years of supervisory or managerial experience). 
Certification/License/Registry:
- Required: None. 
Incentives:
We’re thankful for what you do for us. Here’s what we can do for you:
- This position is performance based annual bonus eligible 
- Sign-on bonus and transition allowance eligible*** 
- Health Insurance (Medical, Dental & Vision) 
- Retirement Contributions Matching Up to 6% [401(a)/403(b)] 
- Annual Raise*** 
- Tuition Reimbursement*** 
- Scholarship Opportunities*** 
- Paid Time Off 
- Childcare (TMH owned onsite facility) 
- Premier Health and Fitness Club (TMH owned offsite facility) 
- Wellness Programs and Colleague Discounts 
- Restrictions may apply
Additional Information:
- Only candidates who meet the requirements will be contacted for further consideration. 
- This vacancy is not eligible for sponsorship. TMH will not sponsor or transfer visas for this position.

Job Title: Director of Operations
Location: Facility
Department: Operations
Reports To: VP’s of Operation, COO
Position Summary
The Director of Operations is responsible for the overall operational performance and strategic implementation of policies, programs, and systems across substance abuse and mental health treatment facilities. This role ensures service excellence, regulatory compliance, fiscal accountability, and employee engagement while driving operational efficiency and enhancing patient experience. The Director works closely with clinical, administrative, and corporate leadership to support the mission of delivering high-quality, evidence-based behavioral health care.  
Key Responsibilities
Operational Oversight
- Direct day-to-day operations across in-patient detox, Residential, and support services.
- Collaborate with Clinical, Nursing, Admissions, HR, and Compliance to ensure alignment of services.
- Develop and implement operational policies and procedures to optimize performance and safety.
- Manage facility licensing and accreditation processes (e.g., Joint Commission, CARF, DCF, SAMHSA).
- Manage overall patient census.
Strategic Leadership
- Assist in developing and executing short- and long-term strategic plans.
- Identify opportunities for program enhancements.
- Participate in decision making and contribute to organizational planning.
Regulatory & Compliance Management
- Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations related to behavioral health, including HIPAA, OSHA, DOH, Joint Commision, CARF, DEA. 
- Lead internal audits and readiness for licensing inspections and third-party reviews.
- Manage Life Safety, Emergency Management, and Environment of Care.
Team Management & Development
- Provide overall leadership and direction for all facility staff, while supervising, mentoring, and developing department managers and administrative leadership.
- Support staff development through coaching, training, and performance management.
- Foster a positive work culture that prioritizes ethics, accountability, and inclusivity.
- Apply best practices in recruiting, hiring, and monitoring the onboarding progress of new hires.
- Ensure that all training and corrective actions are conducted consistently, thoroughly documented, and submitted to Human Resources in a timely manner.  
Quality & Performance Improvement
- Oversee quality assurance initiatives, incident tracking, and risk management.
- Track KPIs related to census, admissions, patient outcomes, and utilization review.
- Use data to implement continuous improvement strategies and drive measurable results.
Financial & Resource Management
- Collaborate with Corporate leadership to develop and monitor departmental budgets, forecasts, and cost-containment strategies.
- Ensure responsible utilization of resources and procurement of operational needs.
- Collaborate with Finance to monitor billing, the Utilization Review department, and financial performance.
- Manage Payroll budgets. 
Patient & Community Engagement
- Promote a patient-centered approach throughout service delivery.
- Referral Management collaboration with business development department. 
- Supervise Patient Care Specialists and oversee discharge planning.
- Maintain company hospitality standards and practices.
Requirements
Qualifications
Required:
- Minimum 3 years of progressive leadership in a behavioral health, substance abuse, or healthcare setting.
- In-depth understanding of behavioral health regulations and operational requirements.
- Demonstrated success in managing multidisciplinary teams.
- Financial proficiency in budget management. 
Preferred:
- Experience with Joint Commission, CARF, state and federal regulatory bodies. 
- Familiarity with state-specific health department regulations (e.g., DCF in Florida).
- Experience with EMR and CRM software.
Core Competencies
- Strategic thinking and execution
- Operational and financial acumen
- Regulatory and compliance expertise
- Crisis management and problem-solving
- Leadership and organizational development
- Communication and relationship building

 At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
About The Operations Team
The Operations team delivers seamless customer experiences and enables new product capabilities while ensuring operational excellence. The team owns strategy, planning, technical execution, customer service, fraud operations, process design, quality, training, and program management. We drive efficiency, resolve issues quickly, and scale operations as the business grows. Our goal is to deliver seamless support while maintaining high standards and reducing risk.
About The Role
Affirm is building a de novo bank, and this role will help establish and scale its operating foundation. You will own the Finxact core and digital banking experience platforms, lead deposit and lending operations strategy, and partner with servicing teams to build resilient, well-controlled processes that deliver transparent, reliable financial products.
What You’ll Do
- Own the implementation, configuration, and ongoing administration of Finxact as the Bank’s core system of record, including product structures, rates and fees, transaction and posting rules, account parameters, general-ledger mappings, user entitlements, environments, and controlled production changes.
- Own the operational delivery and ongoing management of Savana and the Bank’s integrated digital account-opening, online and mobile banking experiences. Translate customer and operational needs into requirements; lead user-acceptance testing, release readiness, issue resolution, and continuous platform improvement.
- Lead operational launch readiness, including operating-model design, procedures, roles and responsibilities, staffing and training, end-to-end testing, mock processing days, cutover, go/no-go evidence, hypercare, and the transition to stable business-as-usual operations.
- Direct daily deposit operations, including balancing Federal Reserve activity to the Finxact ledger; reconciling new-account funding; approving outbound ACH and wire files under dual control; managing inclearing, returns, and exceptions; reviewing failed account boarding; monitoring zero-balance account aging; and overseeing dormancy, escheatment, account maintenance, holds, statements, transaction research, error investigations, dispute resolution, regulatory reporting, and fraud-investigation support.
- Direct lending operations by validating underwriting and eligibility results against Bank guidelines; approving or declining funding within delegated authority; creating and approving funding wires with appropriate segregation of duties; validating loan boarding and journal-entry bookings; and reconciling funding, settlement, daily loan activity, and exceptions.
- Oversee loan purchase and sale operations, including seasoning and eligibility validation, loan-tape and documentation quality control, approval and settlement, confirmation of funds received, accurate sold status and sold-date updates, boarding validation, and completion of purchase and sale audits.
- Build and maintain the Bank’s operational control environment in accordance with Bank-approved policies and independent governance. Own documented procedures, maker-checker controls, reconciliations, access reviews, exception aging, quality assurance, records and evidence, root-cause analysis, issue remediation, and audit and examination readiness; partner with Compliance on BSA/AML, OFAC, consumer-protection, privacy, funds-availability, payments, complaint, and other applicable requirements.
- Manage Bank oversight of affiliate-provided services and critical core, digital banking, payments, document, and operations vendors. Maintain Bank decision rights, data ownership, service levels, audit and remediation rights, and escalation paths; monitor performance, capacity, releases, incidents, and control reports; coordinate root-cause reviews; and maintain tested business-continuity, disaster-recovery, transition, and manual-workaround capabilities.
- Lead and develop a high-performing Bank Operations team through clear decision rights, capacity planning, cross-training, performance management, succession planning, and escalation coverage. Establish metrics for processing timeliness and completeness, reconciliations, exceptions, failed boarding, operational losses, customer-impacting incidents, vendor performance, and control effectiveness, and provide clear reporting and recommendations to Bank leadership.
- Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Accounting, Finance, Treasury, Lending, Compliance, Risk, Information Security, Fraud, Customer Care, Internal Audit, and third parties to design scalable workflows, automate controls, resolve systemic issues, and deliver safe, reliable customer experiences.
What We Look For
- 8+ years of relevant experience in banking operations, digital banking, financial technology, or core-platform delivery, including meaningful experience leading teams and operating in a regulated financial institution.
- Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, converting, or administering a core banking platform; experience with Finxact or another modern cloud-native, API-first core is strongly preferred.
- Experience owning digital account-opening and online or mobile banking platforms and coordinating integrations, user-acceptance testing, releases, production support, and vendor-driven change.
- Deep working knowledge of deposit and lending operations, including ACH, wires, checks and in-clearing, account funding, reconciliations, general-ledger impacts, exception management, loan funding and boarding, and loan purchase or sale settlement.

Job Application for Head of Operations, Intelligence Systems at Anduril Industries
Head of Operations, Intelligence Systems
Reston, Virginia, United StatesApply
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril Intelligence Systems (AIS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Intelligence Community (IC) customers. We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements.
ABOUT THE JOB
We are looking for a Head of Operations to join our rapidly growing Intelligence Systems team. In this role you will be responsible for all business operations for the business line you support. Your work will vary from quick-turn operational fire-fighting, to building and redesigning processes, to leading high-impact strategic projects. This role requires you to be a trusted partner to each part of the business, and to work with and support the Division leadership teams to achieve our strategic objectives.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Partner to the GM — Serve as the right hand to the General Manager of Intelligence Systems, responsible for all internal operations of the business line.
- Act as COO of the business line — Drive day-to-day business operations for Intelligence Systems. This includes business planning & organization design, financial tracking, talent planning & people operations, staffing and hiring, corporate governance, go-to-market, real estate & facility planning, security & infrastructure compliance, proposal & legal support, and sharing the division's narrative — working with cross-functional partners across each of these domains.
- Lead the BizOps team — Lead the Business Operations team within Intelligence Systems, composed of a Business Execution/Services team and Business Analytics, with the potential to include Production Operations/Analytics.
- Own the bottom line — Own the business line P&L and burn rate. Partner with Finance and FP&A to track financial health against division goals, take action to keep operating expenses within budget, and recommend strategies to drive toward margin targets.
- Define growth strategy — Define the growth strategy for Intelligence Systems in partnership with the Intelligence Systems Leadership Team, and lead strategic initiatives in line with business line priorities.
- Enable the engineering mission — Support the growth, execution, and engineering of the business line with operational support.
- Scale the organization — Problem solve to enable the business line to operate as efficiently as possible and scale accordingly.
- Represent the business externally — Build senior leader engagement and external interface strategy (e.g., conferences, press releases, partnerships).
- Build partnerships — Build, negotiate, and execute partnerships across industry.
- Support M&A activity — Identify targets and engage in diligence.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- 10-15+ years of professional experience in operations.
- Strong communication skills; trusted by executives and colleagues alike — Demonstrated ability to translate and articulate thoughts clearly and simply across a wide range of roles (software engineers, finance partners, recruiters, cross-functional leadership, and executives). Communications excellence across a wide dynamic range, both written and verbal. Experience interfacing with company leadership and executives is a must, with a demonstrated ability to cultivate trust, facilitate meetings for, and engage with executives.
- Technically minded — Solid technical aptitude and proven ability to understand technical designs, and the ability to work closely and effectively with engineering teams.
- Bridges operational and analytical teams — Strong emotional intelligence and ability to solve operational problems in a way that is both data-driven and people-centric.
- High ownership and capacity — Horsepower to effectively manage multiple (6+) large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.
- Finance literate — Comfortable owning a bottom line, reading and acting on P&L, budget, and margin data in partnership with FP&A.
- Ability to work onsite five days a week at either our Reston, VA office or our HQ in Costa Mesa, CA.
- Minimum 25% travel expected.
- Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
- MBA or similar degree.
- Experience working with engineers and bringing hardware/software products to market strongly preferred.
- Experience in the intelligence community or national security mission space
- Experience leading a business operations, business analytics, or similar function
- Experience working effectively in a matrix organization structure.
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related field.
US Salary Range
$183,000 - $243,000 USD
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 
Benefits
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:
- 
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
- Please always verify communications:
- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com. 
- 
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
- 
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.
Data Privacy
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/. 
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. What We’re Looking For
At GNC we embrace a “Live Well” philosophy, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation meets passion. Whether someone is an athlete or just starting to focus on their health, we want to deliver the cutting-edge products they deserve. We are looking for an individual who is excited and eager to play a pivotal role in driving excellence in the health and wellness industry. This position offers the opportunity to engage in a collaborative environment where you will make a personal impact every day.
The Director of Franchise Operations at GNC is a key leadership role responsible for the growth, development, and operational excellence of franchise partners within their respective markets. This role involves close collaboration with franchisees to maximize their success and profitability, ensure adherence to GNC's operating system and standards, and maintain a consistent, high-quality customer experience across the franchise network. The Director also plays a critical role in driving both retail and wholesale revenues and is responsible for mentoring franchisees in all aspects of training and operations. This position will oversee franchise locations mainly in Florida, with other locations in Alabama, Mississippi, and Louisiana.

This is a Full-Time Salary Position

 Franchisee Relationship Management:

- Facilitate communication and collaboration between franchisees and various GNC support departments (e.g., Merchandising, Marketing, Finance, Real Estate, Legal, Science, Product Development).
- Build and maintain strong, productive relationships with franchisees, providing guidance, coaching, and support to enhance their success in maximizing their profitability.

- Coach franchisees to maximize their return on investment and operational performance.

- Oversee the completion of Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III training programs for new franchisees.

- Implement dispute resolution methods to address differences and maintain positive relationships with franchisees.

 The Company
Zurn Elkay Water Solutions Corporation is a thriving, values-driven company focused on doing the right things. We’re a fast growing, publicly traded company (NYSE: ZWS), with an enduring reputation for integrity, giving back, and providing an engaging, inclusive environment where careers flourish and grow.
Named by Newsweek as One of America’s Most Responsible Companies and an Energage USA Top Workplace, at Zurn Elkay Water Solutions Corporation, we never forget that our people are at the center of what makes us successful. They are the driving force behind our superior quality, product ingenuity, and exceptional customer experience. Our commitment to our people and their professional development is a recipe for success that has fueled our growth for over 100 years, as one of today’s leading international suppliers of plumbing and water delivery solutions.
Headquartered in Milwaukee, WI, Zurn Elkay Water Solutions Corporation employs over 2800 employees worldwide, working from 24 locations across the U.S., China, Canada, Dubai, and Mexico, with sales offices available around the globe. We hope you’ll visit our website and learn more about Zurn Elkay at zurnelkay.com.
If you’re ready to join a company where what you do makes a difference and you have pride in the work you are doing, talk to us about joining the Zurn Elkay Water Solutions Corporation family!
If you are a current employee, please navigate here to apply internally.
The Business Director – ZEBS leads operational excellence initiatives to deliver relevant business objectives. This position acts as a strategic thought partner to the dotted line business leader, drives accelerated commercial and financial performance to meet business objectives in revenue, EBITDA, and other relevant financial metrics, and provides strategic leadership with hands-on implementation of both Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies to drive performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and associate engagement.
- Serve as a key member of the Business leadership team identifying opportunities to improve or accelerate business objectives; sharing best practices; and developing, implementing, and standardizing processes in both commercial and manufacturing operations
- Work with VP/GM of Business Units and other functional leaders as a “thought leader” to define current state situation, assess gaps in process/capabilities/talent, and assist in development of the future state in line with strategic plan
- Ensure successful definition and execution of large, cross-functional improvement initiatives tied to annual strategic priorities
- Directly support teams to achieve strategic objectives by conducting on-site workshops, Kaizen events, training, and providing guidance through the transformation process
- Assist teams in developing a roadmap to use in the deployment of strategic objectives as they relate to Sales growth, Share gains, value propositions, New Product Launch/Commercialization and Problem solving
- Coach and mentor business managers and associates in the use of various tools, concepts and practices around ZEBS commercial processes (Daily/Visual Management, Sales and Opportunity Funnel Management, Plan for Every Rep [PFER], and other relevant tools as needed)
- Partner with ZEBS Director – Commercial Operations to identify and share best practices across Zurn Elkay businesses, drive process implementation and adherence, and drive a culture of process rigor throughout the assigned business commercial function
- Work with direct reports to develop and execute site-wide continuous improvement roadmaps, integrating Lean principles and methodologies (e.g., Kaizen, VDM, 5S, TPM, SMED) into all levels of the organization
- Partner closely with Plant Managers and functional leaders to align daily execution with strategic business goals
- Champion a culture of operational excellence through coaching, training, and mentoring of direct reports, leaders and associates on Lean tools, problem-solving, and waste elimination
- Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams to improve production flow, increase equipment uptime, and optimize resource utilization
Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred
- 10+ years of experience with at least 5 years in operational excellence with demonstrated success in both commercial and operations; line experience in commercial (5+ years sales, product management, marketing) or manufacturing (5+ years manufacturing leadership) preferred
- Proven track record implementing Lean methodologies and driving measurable operational improvement
- Excellent communication, presentation, and facilitation skills
- Ability to lead through influence, engage teams, and drive cultural change
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
- Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) preferred
- Travel up to 50%

Job Application for Senior Manager of Digital Quality Systems at Anduril Industries
Senior Manager of Digital Quality Systems
Costa Mesa, California, United StatesApply
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril’s Quality organization is seeking a Senior Manager, Digital Quality Systems to lead the team responsible for our digital quality platform and analytics infrastructure. The Quality team works with our customers, internal teams, and suppliers to ensure the deployment of reliable products that meet all mission requirements. We develop cutting-edge quality processes and methods to secure scalable, long-term business success. We are growing rapidly across multiple product lines and sites, and this role will own the quality workflows inside Forge, our homegrown Manufacturing Execution System, and the Quality Intelligence Hub, our centralized analytics and compliance layer built on Databricks. The right person for this role lives at the intersection of software and quality engineering, someone who can design a data model, review code, ship in sprints, and understand how nonconformance, CAPA, and inspection processes work on a real factory floor. If you want to build the digital quality backbone for the next generation of defense manufacturing, this is the seat.
This role is subject to ITAR. Applicants must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Platform architecture. Own the design of quality workflows in Forge: inspection routings, data capture points, decision logic and audit trails. Keep them version-controlled and audit-ready.
- Core quality workflows. Build NC, disposition, containment, CAPA, SCAR and inspection instructions into production flow, not bolted on after it.
- Quality Intelligence Hub. Direct the data models and dashboards behind FPY, DPU, escape rates, CAPA aging, NC Pareto, supplier scorecards and SPC trending.
- Operator experience. Make sure floor operators and quality engineers get fast, error-resistant tools they actually want to use.
- Team leadership. Lead developers, data engineers, analysts and quality SMEs: set sprint priorities, review designs and code, and unblock decisions.
- Cross-functional alignment. Keep the platform in step with product development, supplier quality, reliability and manufacturing as programs and sites scale.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent hands-on software experience.
- 10+ years building or leading enterprise software, manufacturing systems or quality systems, with 5+ years leading engineers or analysts.
- Hands-on software credibility: you can sketch an architecture, challenge a schema, read a pull request and make build-vs-buy calls.
- Working knowledge of enterprise quality processes: NC, CAPA, SCAR, disposition, containment, inspection and document control, and how each translates into data capture and workflow.
- Data and analytics fluency: SQL and Python, and experience with a modern data platform such as Databricks, Snowflake or similar.
- Experience running agile delivery: sprint planning, backlog grooming, CI/CD and iterative releases with a cross-functional team.
- Comfort making architecture decisions with imperfect information in a fast-scaling environment.
- U.S. citizenship is required pursuant to contractual obligations.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Experience with a homegrown or heavily customized MES, not only out-of-the-box SAP QM or Windchill.
- Aerospace, defense, medical device or other regulated manufacturing background (AS9100, ISO 9001, ISO 13485).
- Practical AI/ML use in production workflows or strong personal fluency with AI tooling.
- Statistical methods in practice: SPC, MSA and process capability analysis.
- IoT-enabled inspection data capture, automated optical inspection or machine vision integration.
- APQP/PPAP or FMEA tied into digital quality systems.
- ASQ certification (CQE, CMQ/OE or Six Sigma Black Belt).

$191,000 - $254,000 USD

Benefits
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:
- 
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
- Please always verify communications:
- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
- 
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

Exceptional Hospitality Starts with You
Picture yourself brightening someone’s day. When you join our Hotels team, that’s exactly what you’ll do every time you come to work! As a Property Operations Director, you’re not just responsible for the safety and functionality of the property – you’re spreading the light and warmth of hospitality by delivering memorable experiences that make the stay for every guest.
Responsibilities
Here's what you'll do during a typical day:
- Lead facility operations: Direct the functionality, safety, and compliance of the hotel’s buildings, mechanical systems, electrical systems, HVAC, life safety systems, and grounds in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations
- Oversee facility maintenance: Conduct facility inspections, maintain documentation for energy management and conservation programs, and oversee preventive maintenance initiatives
- Direct property improvements: Lead capital projects and property rehabilitations – including scheduling, budgeting, contractor bidding, and licensing/permitting – while ensuring regulatory compliance
- Drive operational excellence: Direct daily department operations, including guest service initiatives, product quality, inventory management, budgeting, forecasting, and adherence to industry standards
- Cultivate a high-performing team: Drive engagement and retention through performance management, professional development, and recognition programs
Qualifications
What It Takes to Make the Stay
At Hilton, Our Core Values Define What It Takes To Succeed Here And Guide The Qualities We Look For In Every Team Member
A passion for spreading the light and warmth of Hospitality. Acting with Integrity and always doing the right thing. Inspiring others through Leadership. A belief that Teamwork drives the best outcomes. A sense of Ownership and accountability. And a focus on the Now, bringing urgency and discipline to every moment, knowing it can make a lasting impact.
About Us
Join an Award-Winning Workplace Culture
At Hilton, we don’t just deliver exceptional experiences for our guests—we build an exceptional workplace for the Team Members who make it all possible. As a global leader in hospitality, we’ve welcomed more than 3 billion guests worldwide, all while staying true to our founding vision: to fill the earth with the light and warmth of hospitality.
Our award-winning culture has earned us repeated recognition on the World’s Best Workplaces list by Great Place to Work and Fortune. With our suite of world-class brands , and a company-wide commitment to providing the best stay for every guest, we’re setting new standards for the future of travel.
Whether you’re starting your career or exploring something new, Hilton supports your journey every step of the way. Come for the job, stay for the career—and help us make every stay a little more magical.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.
At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.
Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.
Group Overview
Special Air Missions Group - US (SAM - US) is responsible for developing and delivering Metrea’s ISR, Special Mobility, and Aerial Firefighting (AFF) capabilities. SAM US oversees the integration of new mission systems, ensuring operational readiness across specialized aviation operations. It manages fleet maintenance, regulatory compliance, and strategic partnerships to enhance mission effectiveness. By consolidating expertise and infrastructure, SAM - US ensures Metrea’s airborne capabilities remain adaptable and mission-ready across dynamic operational environments. 
Position Summary
Reporting to the Head of Aerial Firefighting Operations, the Head of Crew Training is responsible for the development, recruitment, selection, qualification, standardization, and continuous improvement of the organization's flight crew training system in support of compliant, safe, reliable, effective, efficient, and evolvable (CSRE³) flight operations.
Within the Metrea Management System, the Head of Crew Training fulfills the role comparable to an AFF Chief Pilot, an EASA Nominated Person for Crew Training, and a CASA Head of Training and Checking. This role is responsible for ensuring pilots, Airborne Mission Operators/Coordinators, and other assigned flight crew members are properly selected, trained, qualified, current, and competent to safely execute Part 137 AFF Operations wherever that standard is accepted by the National Aviation Authority (NAA). It may also be necessary to support third party operators or partners in the execution of their operational approvals e.g. CAR702 in Canada.
The Head of Crew Training leads aircrew recruitment, training, qualification, and standardization programs, manages training resources and records, and ensures training programs remain aligned with regulatory requirements, operational risk, mission requirements, and emerging operational capabilities. The role also supports operational test and evaluation, mission system integration, and Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTP) development to ensure new capabilities are effectively transitioned into operational service.
What You'll Do
- Lead the aircrew lifecycle, including recruitment, selection, onboarding, training, qualification, standardization, and professional development of pilots, Airborne Sensor Operators, and other assigned flight crew members
- Establish, implement, and continuously improve aircrew qualification standards, training syllabi, evaluation criteria, and standardization programs that support compliant, safe, reliable, effective, efficient, and evolvable (CSRE³) flight operations
- Recruit, develop, and oversee the standardization cadre, ensuring consistent application of training and operational standards and TTP across the organization
- Manage enterprise training resources, qualification records, learning management systems, simulators, training aircraft, and other training assets to support operational readiness
- Monitor and evaluate training effectiveness through assessments, audits, operational feedback, qualification trends, and performance metrics, implementing continuous improvement initiatives where appropriate
- Promote Safety Management System (SMS) principles and operational risk management throughout all training activities, ensuring training reflects current operational procedures, hazards, and risk mitigation
- Lead operational test and evaluation, developmental testing, validation, verification, and TTP development for new aircraft capabilities, mission systems, sensors, and operational concepts, ensuring new capabilities are effectively integrated into operational training and standardization 
- Coordinate Flight Operations, Safety, Compliance, Security, Maintenance, the Continuous Airworthiness Management Organization, the Aerospace Engineering Group, the People Group, and operational leadership to ensure aircrew readiness, workforce planning, and training programs remain aligned with organizational priorities and operational requirements. What You Bring
- Bachelor's degree in Aviation, Aviation Management, Education, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent operational aviation leadership experience
- Commercial Aircraft Multi-Engine Land Pilot Certificate with Instrument Rating, appropriate aircraft type ratings, and qualifications required to serve as a Pilot-in-Command and Standardization Captain in DHC8-300 aircraft
- Minimum five years of aviation leadership experience, including at least two years in flight crew training, standardization, or operational leadership
- Demonstrated experience leading aerial firefighting crew recruitment, selection, qualification, instructor development, and enterprise training programs
- Practical experience applying aviation safety standards, Safety Management Systems (SMS), and operational risk management principles
- Comprehensive knowledge of applicable FAA, US Wildland Fire Service and other AFF regulatory requirements governing flight operations and crew training
- Experience supporting operational test and evaluation, flight test, mission system integration, or development of operational TTPs preferred
- Strong leadership, organizational, strategic thinking, communication, and workforce development skills
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Learning Management Systems (LMS), and training management software
- Ability to deploy in support of operations, training, standardization, evaluations, and test activities

Take your next career step at ABB E-mobility with a global team that is energizing the transformation of society and industry toward a more productive, sustainable future. As Head of Public Charging for North America, you will own the commercial strategy, the key customer relationships, and the growth agenda that will determine whether ABB becomes the leading public charging infrastructure partner across the U.S. and Canada.
This is not a traditional sales leadership role. You will shape how an entire segment goes to market, build long-term partnerships with the most important charge point operators in North America, and lead the kind of complex, high-stake deals that genuinely move markets. Reporting to the Global Head of Public Charging, you will have the autonomy to set your strategy while drawing on the full resources and expertise of ABB E-mobility's global organization.
If you are a commercially sharp, execution-focused leader with a strong feel for the public charging market and the drive to own a critical business in one of the fastest-growing sectors in the world, this role is for you.
Location: Charlotte, NC, with travel across North America
In This Role Your Main Accountabilities Will Be
- Own the Commercial P&L: You are accountable for delivering orders, revenue, and gross profit across ultra-high-power, high-power, and destination charging in North America. Profitable, scalable growth is the goal, not volume for its own sake.
- Define and Execute the Go-to-Market Strategy: You are the architect of how ABB wins in North America. You decide which customers we serve directly, which we reach through partners, and where our commercial resources create the most leverage.
- Lead the Most Strategic Customer Relationships Personally: You personally own the relationships with our most important charge point operators in North America. You build account-specific strategies, activate executive sponsorship, and lead the win-back agenda where it is needed.
- Match ABB's Full Portfolio to Customer Use Cases: You are the commercial bridge to customers across hardware, software, energy management, and long-term service. 
- Drive Pricing Discipline and Margin Integrity: You own pricing governance, TCO-based selling, and service attach strategy. Growth never comes at the expense of profitability or downstream service risk.
- Own Forecasting, Pipeline and Business Governance: You are expected to provide a consistent, accurate view of orders, revenue, gross profit, pipeline coverage, and competitive position. You create transparency and confidence across Commercial, Product, Operations, Service, and Finance.
- Build a High-Performing Commercial Team: You are the one who builds a team of genuine segment specialists. You create the account planning, forecasting, and execution rhythm that allows the business to scale without unnecessary complexity.
- Lead the Shift to Scalable, Repeatable Execution: You are responsible for moving the business from bespoke deal-making to blueprint-based execution. You hold stakeholders across Product, Operations, Finance, and Supply Chain accountable to that standard.
- Strengthen the Channel and Partner Ecosystem: You work closely with the North America Channel team to build a focused, high-quality partner network. Clear rules, clear expectations, and clear productivity targets are your standard.
- Shape the Market Perception of ABB: You represent ABB externally with customers, partners, public agencies, and industry coalitions. You are a credible voice on reliability, uptime, site economics, energy management, battery integration, cable-theft mitigation, long-term service models, and high-power infrastructure.
We are looking for a senior commercial leader who brings:
- 12+ years of commercial leadership experience, ideally in EV charging, energy systems, electrical infrastructure, or another complex B2B technology environment
- A proven track record of scaling a business or revenue line of $100M or more
- Real experience leading enterprise key accounts and winning large infrastructure or technology programs in competitive markets
- Strong skills in TCO-based selling, pricing governance, and structuring hardware plus software plus service deals, with the executive presence to bring these conversations credibly to C-level
- A solid understanding of the North American public charging ecosystem including CPOs, utilities, NEVI funding, and high-power infrastructure trends
- Familiarity with fleet operators, retailers, and public funding dynamics such as NEVI is a strong plus
- Experience working across direct, partner-led, and channel-led go-to-market models
- A track record of competitive displacement in fast-moving markets and the ability to hold cross-functional stakeholders accountable without creating bureaucracy
Beyond the experience, we are looking for someone with a high ownership mindset, who leads with clarity and urgency, holds themselves accountable before anyone else does, and knows how to rebuild trust where it needs rebuilding. Someone who is really energized by transformation, not just comfortable with it.
What’s in it for you?
Work with the best specialists in their field, in a diverse environment with unparalleled global reach. Feel inspired by our fast growth. You will have the accountability to own your part in enabling a future of sustainable and efficient mobility. You can also count on a competitive compensation package in line with your capabilities and experience. Diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunities are at the core of what we do. We celebrate different experiences and perspectives, and we aim to empower everyone in the creation of sustainable solutions for people all over the world. Our individual differences make us successful. 
About ABB E-Mobility 
ABB E-mobility is a global leader in EV charging infrastructure, across the full spectrum of public charging infrastructure. Our modular architecture, energy management platform, and service capabilities give us a real commercial edge in a market where customers are increasingly choosing partners based on uptime, scalability, and long-term operating economics, not hardware alone.
North America is one of the most important battlegrounds for the future of public charging, and this role sits at the center of it. The competitive window is wide open and our technology is ready. The right leader can shape how this market will develop.

General Manager
*Candidates whose experience is primarily within the landscape industry will not be considered for this particular opportunity.*
Location: Orlando, FL
We are Sunrise Landscape, an established commercial landscape organization for more than 40 years across the state of Florida. We are excited by our vision to deliver excellent customer service in the areas of landscape design, installation and maintenance to our clients with the help of our 1,000+ employees. We are proud to have achieved the Lawn & Landscape Top 100 honor and are continuing to build a great place to work with a commitment to landscape and service excellence.
Do you want to be part of a hardworking, driven team where your contributions make an impact every day? We’re excited to welcome a General Manager, Operations to our team in Orlando, FL!
While we are a commercial landscape organization, for this position, we are intentionally seeking candidates from outside the landscape industry. We are looking for leaders who bring fresh perspectives, proven operational discipline, and experience leading complex, service driven businesses with large frontline workforces. Candidates whose experience is primarily within the landscape industry will not be considered for this particular opportunity.
We strongly encourage candidates from industries such as facilities services, field services, construction services, logistics, distribution, manufacturing, hospitality operations, or other single site/service-based environments to apply.
Position Summary
The General Manager, Maintenance Operations is responsible for the overall operational, financial, and strategic performance of an assigned branch or geographic area within the Maintenance division. This role serves as the senior operational leader for the location and has full accountability for profitability, client retention, employee engagement, and execution of company initiatives.
This position is designed to have a significant impact on the organization’s growth, both organically and through acquisitions. The General Manager leads teams responsible for daily landscape maintenance operations while ensuring exceptional service delivery, disciplined financial management, strong client relationships, and a culture of safety and accountability.
A successful General Manager is a highly analytical, detail-oriented operational leader with a proven track record of maximizing profitability in a service-based business, leading multi-functional teams through growth and change, and driving operational excellence.
What You'll Own:
As General Manager, you'll operate your branches like it's your own business. The two branches have approximately 80 team members supporting clients in our landscape maintenance division (recurring service for commercial clients). The two branches are located in Casselberry, FL and Winter Garden, FL.
Key Responsibilities
As one of our General Managers, Maintenance Operations, you will have the following areas of responsibility:
Financial & Business Performance
- Own and deliver branch financial results, including profitability, maintenance revenue growth, and enhancement revenue growth, in alignment with established goals and incentive plans
- Develop, manage, and maintain full P&L responsibility for the branch or assigned geographic area, ensuring disciplined expense control and sustainable margin performance
- Analyze financial and operational performance metrics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for cost optimization and revenue growth
- Establish and execute annual operating plans and budgets aligned with company objectives
Operations Leadership
- Oversee all operational aspects of the branch or assigned geographic area, including field operations, service delivery, fleet management, and vendor partnerships
- Lead daily service execution, including crew direction, scheduling, and allocation of people and equipment resources
- Ensure landscape contracts are executed to scope, quality, and service standards while maintaining high client retention rates
- Identify operational challenges and implement scalable, effective solutions that improve efficiency and service quality
Client & Account Management
- Lead and support Account Managers in building and maintaining strong client relationships
- Address escalated client issues promptly and professionally, ensuring resolution and long-term satisfaction
- Partner with Sales and Account Management to participate in client meetings, proposals, renewals, and contract negotiations
- Drive a client-centric culture focused on responsiveness, accountability, and value delivery
People Leadership
- Lead, develop, and retain high-performing teams, including Client Relationship Managers, Operations Managers, service delivery crews, and support staff
- Train qualified team members to meet current and future business needs
- Provide ongoing coaching, performance feedback, and development to build leadership capability and bench strength
- Foster a positive, inclusive, and accountable work environment aligned with company values and culture
- Support employee engagement initiatives that strengthen retention, performance, and team culture
Safety, Compliance & Process Excellence
- Champion safety initiatives and ensure compliance with all company, local, state, and federal safety requirements
- Promote a safety-first mindset and maintain a safe, healthy work environment for all employees
- Execute and enforce company policies, procedures, and operational standards consistently across the branch or assigned geographic area
- Ensure operational processes align with broader organizational goals and continuous improvement efforts
- Resolve customer and vendor issues effectively while maintaining strong business relationships
Qualifications & Core Competencies
- Ten to fifteen years of progressive leadership experience with a strong emphasis on operations management
- Bachelor’s degree required
- Demonstrated success leading and developing teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and accountability
- Strong financial acumen with proven experience managing full P&L responsibility
- Ability to analyze complex operational and financial data and translate insights into action
- Proven ability to resolve customer and vendor issues while elevating the overall client experience
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and influencing skills with diverse employee groups and external stakeholders
- High degree of professionalism, discretion, and integrity, including the ability to handle confidential information
- Experience using operational and financial software tools to track performance and optimize efficiency
- Previous experience in the landscape or similar service-based industry preferred
- Entrepreneurial mindset with a bias toward action and continuous improvement
Driver Qualifications
To qualify as a Driver, in addition to the above, you must:
- Possess a valid driver’s license issued in the United States for a minimum of three years
- Maintain a clean driving record for at least three years
- Successfully pass a drug screening

We are committed to providing a workplace where you can develop your skills, advance your career, contribute to a high-performing team, and do meaningful work alongside people who embody our core values of accountability, resilience, and collaboration. Description
THE PURPOSE: This role is responsible for leading bulk production execution for True Religion’s denim business, ensuring approved product is manufactured to quality standards and delivered on time. The Director owns factory production performance, capacity planning, order execution, and the proactive resolution of risks that may impact deliveries or business commitments, working closely with Product Development, Technical Design, Merchandising, Logistics, and Sourcing to drive accountability across suppliers and internal teams. The ideal candidate will play a key role in improving delivery reliability through disciplined production management, strong factory partnerships, and continuous process improvement, and contribute to True Religion’s continued growth by protecting margins across the denim business.
THE ROLE (what you are accountable for):
- 
Production Ownership & On-Time Delivery: Lead denim bulk production from approved production handoff through shipment, ensuring purchase orders meet agreed quality standards, ship windows, and delivery commitments.
- 
Factory Capacity & Production Planning: Validate factory capacity, material readiness, and production schedules against seasonal and chase demand. Secure realistic production commitments and proactively address capacity constraints.
- 
Vendor Performance & Accountability: Manage manufacturing partners and hold factories accountable for accurate status reporting, production milestones, quality, and on-time shipment. Escalate performance gaps and drive measurable corrective actions.
- 
Production Calendar & Critical Path: Own production time-and-action calendars, monitor key milestones from purchase order placement through ex-factory, and resolve delays before they impact the distribution center (DC) delivery plan.
- 
Quality & Manufacturing Execution: Partner with Technical Design, Quality, and Product Development to ensure factories execute approved specifications, construction, washes, and finishing standards, and drive timely resolution of bulk production issues.
- 
Cost Protection & Operational Efficiency: Protect approved product costs by managing production changes, minimizing rework and avoidable airfreight, and identifying manufacturing efficiencies without compromising quality or delivery.
- 
Risk Management & Recovery: Identify risks related to fabric, trims, washing, factory output, inspections, and shipping readiness. Develop and execute recovery plans with clear owners, timelines, and business impact.
- 
Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner with Product Development, Merchandising, Planning, Technical Design, Sourcing, and Logistics to align on buy changes, reorder needs, production priorities, and delivery expectations.
- 
Reporting & Business Visibility: Provide timely, accurate updates on purchase order status, production forecasts, late-order exposure, factory performance, and recovery plans, communicating material risks early with actionable recommendations.
- 
Team Leadership & Process Improvement: Lead and develop the denim production team, including the Production Managers for Mainline and OP, establishing clear accountability and operating routines, strengthening factory management processes, and improving production reliability and speed to market.
YOU ARE: You bring a strong combination of denim manufacturing expertise and hands-on production leadership. You understand denim factory operations, wash and finishing processes, capacity planning, quality control, and the impact of execution decisions on cost and delivery. You are proactive, decisive, and highly accountable, with the ability to challenge factory commitments, anticipate risks, and drive solutions before they affect the business. You build strong relationships, lead teams with clear expectations, and thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
REQUIRED MINIMUM EXPERIENCE
10+ years of denim production experience, including 2-4+ years in a leadership role
Deep knowledge of denim manufacturing, including factory operations, wash and finishing processes, and quality control
Proven experience managing bulk production from production handoff through shipment, including time-and-action calendars and critical path management
Track record of holding factories accountable for capacity, quality, and on-time delivery
Experience protecting product costs by managing production changes, rework, and airfreight
Strong reporting skills, with the ability to communicate order status, risks, and recovery plans clearly to leadership
Experience leading and developing production teams
Ability to partner cross-functionally and make sound decisions quickly in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: 
- Experience developing both men's and women's denim programs, including core and fashion styles.
- Experience with international factory networks, wash facilities, and high-volume production.
- Familiarity with ERP/PLM systems, vendor scorecards, and production KPI reporting.

Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including relevant experience, skills, knowledge, and internal equity.

Perks: We offer a mix of benefits and perks to support our employees at work and beyond, including health benefits, a 401(k) with employer match, merchandise discounts, commuter benefits, wellness & employee assistance programs, and more.

Following the initial transition period, the role will move to a hybrid work model of four days per week in the office and one remote day, with an expectation of in-office presence on designated days to support collaboration and business needs.

Job Description
Job Summary:
The Director of Quality is a strategic leader responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving the organization’s quality management systems. This role ensures products, services, and processes meet regulatory requirements, industry standards, and customer expectations while driving a culture of quality, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the enterprise.
Key Responsibilities
Leadership & Strategy
- Develop and execute a comprehensive quality strategy aligned with organizational goals.
- Serve as a key member of the leadership team, advising on quality risks, compliance, and performance.
- Build and lead high-performing quality teams across multiple locations or business units.
- Promote a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Quality Management Systems (QMS)
- Oversee the design, implementation, and maintenance of the Quality Management System (e.g., ISO, FDA, or industry-specific standards).
- Ensure compliance with all applicable regulatory and certification requirements.
- Lead internal and external audits, inspections, and certifications.
- Establish and maintain quality policies, procedures, and documentation.
Process Improvement & Operational Excellence
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies.
- Analyze quality data and metrics to identify trends, root causes, and opportunities for improvement.
- Partner with Operations, Engineering, and Supply Chain to improve process efficiency and product quality.
- Lead corrective and preventive action (CAPA) processes.
Customer & Supplier Quality
- Ensure customer quality requirements and expectations are consistently met or exceeded.
- Oversee customer complaint resolution and root cause analysis.
- Manage supplier quality programs, including qualification, performance monitoring, and audits.
- Strengthen supplier partnerships to ensure consistent materials and service standards.
Risk Management & Compliance
- Identify quality-related risks and implement mitigation strategies.
- Ensure compliance with all regulatory bodies and applicable laws.
- Lead risk assessments (FMEA, HACCP, etc., depending on industry).
- Maintain readiness for regulatory inspections and audits.
Reporting & Metrics
- Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for quality performance.
- Provide regular executive-level reporting on quality trends, risks, and improvements.
- Use data-driven insights to support strategic decision-making.
Qualifications
Education
- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Life Sciences, or related field required.
- Master’s degree (MBA or technical discipline) preferred.
Experience
- 10+ years of progressive experience in quality management, including 5+ years in a leadership role.
- Experience in manufacturing, aerospace.
- Proven track record of implementing and improving QMS frameworks.
- Strong experience with regulatory and compliance standards (e.g., ISO 9001, FDA, GMP, etc.).
Certifications (Preferred)
- ASQ Certified Quality Manager (CQM) or similar.
- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.
Pay & Benefits
For informational purposes only, the range for annual base salary for this role is $170000 to $256000 US Dollar (USD) Salaried based on a variety of factors. For informational purposes only, this role is eligible to participate in the Company’s Executive Bonus Plan, paid out up to 30% of the applicable annual base salary, based on the Company’s performance in the prior calendar year. Employees will receive 120 hours paid time off every year. Employees will also receive 10 paid holidays. Employees (and their families) are eligible to participate in the company's medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s 401(k) plan.
Relocation is authorized for this position.
National Security And Export Controls
This position requires use of information or access to production processes subject to national security controls under U.S. export control laws and regulations (including, but not limited to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR)). To comply with those regulations, this position may require applicants to be U.S. Persons (i.e., U.S. citizens, U.S. lawful permanent residents, protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)), or eligible to obtain the required export authorizations from the U.S. Department of State or the U.S. Department of Commerce.
About PCC
With more than 120 operations and approximately 20,000 employees worldwide, Precision Castparts Corp. is the market leader in manufacturing large, complex structural investment castings, airfoil castings, forged components, aerostructures and highly engineered, critical fasteners for aerospace applications. In addition, we are the leading producer of airfoil castings for the industrial gas turbine market. We also manufacture extruded seamless pipe, fittings, and forgings for power generation and oil & gas applications; commercial and military airframe aerostructures; and metal alloys and other materials for the casting and forging industries. With such critical applications, we insist on quality and dependability – not just in the materials and products we make, but in the people we recruit.
PCC is relentless in its dedication to being a high-quality, low-cost and on-time producer; delivering the highest value to its customers while continually pursuing strategic, profitable growth.
In 2016, Berkshire Hathaway, led by Chairman and CEO Warren E. Buffett, acquired Precision Castparts Corp.
